newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower after ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower after ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly lower Tuesday, as traders shaved some strength off August on ACCESS, industry sources said.
On ACCESS, August last traded a half cent lower at $2.063.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.055 to $2.065 after settling to the downside Monday at $2.068 per million British thermal units.
Early cash prices were still talked steady at $2.11-2.13 at the Henry Hub.
Technical traders said support in August was still at $2.05-2.055, and then at $2. Resistance was pegged at $2.11-2.12, $2.15 and then along the down trendline around $2.26.

Cash prices held their premium to futures on Monday despite moderate weather across most of the U.S. Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents to about $2.10, while Midcon pipes were little changed in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also was quoted a couple of cents higher in the high-$2.30s.
Continuing to support cash, traders said, was the strong demand in the West as hot, humid weather blanketed most of the Southwest and storage levels still lagged behind year-ago tallies.
Early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 74 bcf.
